G. Sreeramulu vs Dr. Venkateswarlu, Ias on 13 December, 2024 
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao
 Contempt Case No.1373 Of 2024
Order: 
(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao) This Contempt Case is filed complaining of disobedience of the order dated 05.07.2023 passed by this Court in I.A.No.1 of 2017 (Rev.W.P.M.P.No.26423 of 2017) in W.P.No.8808 of 2016. 
2. The Petitioner was initially appointed as a Health Assistant in the Medical and Health Department in the year 1990; subsequently, he was appointed by transfer as Sanitary Inspector in the Panchayat Raj Department in the year 1997. He has acquired the qualification and undergone training for appointment to the post of Food Inspector (Non-Gazetted). While so, the petitioner filed W.P.No.8808 of 2016 seeking the following relief :-
"..... to grant appropriate relief more in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring Proceedings Rc.No. 2467/E1/2014-15, dated 01.04.2015 issued by the 1st 2 AKS,J &
RRN,J Respondent and consequential proceedings Rc.No. 80/AFC/Z-IV/2015, dated 07.04.2015 issued by the 3rd respondent as arbitrary, illegal, discriminatory,
malafide, void and without jurisdiction apart from violating Articles 14, 16 and 21 of the Constitution of India and set aside the same including the orders of the Hon'ble Tribunal dated 20th August 2015 in O.A.No.4438/2015 and orders of the Hon'ble Tribunal dated 9th November 2015 in Review MA No.2523/2015 in O.A.No.4438/2015 as arbitrary as well as erroneous and issue consequential directions directing the Respondents to allow the Petitioner to continue as Food Inspector/Food Safety Officer Non-Gazetted with all consequential benefits and issue gazette notification to that effect and pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble High Court deems fit and proper in the circumstances of the case." 
3. After hearing the matter, this Court dismissed the Writ Petition on 28.04.2017. Against the said order, the petitioner filed I.A.No.1 of 2017 (Rev.W.P.M.P.No.26423 of 2017) in W.P.No.8808 of 2016 seeking to review the order dated 28.04.2017 passed by this Court in W.P.No.8808 of 2016. 
The said review petition was allowed on 05.07.2023 by observing as follows :-
3 AKS,J & RRN,J "This Court, having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, is of the view that the review petitioner was promoted G. Sreeramulu vs Dr. Venkateswarlu, Ias on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47212770/
1 to the post of Food Inspector pursuant to Memo, dated. 03-09-2014, issued by the State Government, and the Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare being subordinate to the State Government could not have passed reversion order,
dated.01.04.2015. Therefore, the order, dated.28.04.2017, passed by this Court in W.P.No.8808 of 2016 as well as the order, dated 20.08.2015, passed by the Tribunal in O.A.No. 4438 of 2015 and the reversion order, dated.01.04.2015, passed by the Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare, are liable to be set aside and accordingly, they are set aside. 
Accordingly, the review petition is allowed."
4. In compliance with the above order, the respondents have issued proceedings dated 02.09.2023 stating as follows :-
"....As per the orders of the Hon'ble Court of Telangana at Hyderabad dated.15.07.2023 Sri. G.Sreeramulu, presently working as Sanitary Inspector is appointed by transfer (by promotion) to the post of Food Safety Officer(formerly Food Inspector (Non-Gazetted) under the administrative control of the Commissioner of Food Safety, Andhra Pradesh, under Rule 11(b) of the A.P. State 4 AKS,J & RRN,J Subordinate Service Rules, 1996 in the time scale of Rs.45830-130580. 
Sri. G.Sreeramulu, Sanitary Inspector, Gram Panchyat, Bhattiprolu, Bapatla District is informed that appointed by transfer (by promotion) as Food Inspector (Non-Gazetted)/Food Safety Officer is purely on temporary basis and he is liable to be repatriated at any time to his original post in his parent Department without any notice and without assigning any reasons thereof. He is also informed that the appointed by transfer (by promotion) as Food Inspector (Non Gazetted)/Food Safety Officer is subject to the final outcome of OAS/WPs and disciplinary cases, if any,
pending before the Hon'ble Court....". 
5. After issuance of the above said proceedings, the petitioner has filed the present Contempt Case. 
6. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that after allowing the Review Petition by this Court, the respondents have issued posting orders as Food Safety Inspector, which position the petitioner was already holding prior to the passing of the impugned order of reversion. The 5 AKS,J & RRN,J respondents have not given any consequential benefits that flow from setting aside the impugned order of reversion. 
7. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner further submits that the respondents ought to have not only restored the position of the petitioner as Food Safety Inspector but also ought to have granted all consequential benefits, including reckoning of the seniority of the petitioner in the cadre of Food Safety Inspector from the date of appointment in the promotional post as Food Safety Inspector and also ought to have considered for further higher promotion. The action of the G. Sreeramulu vs Dr. Venkateswarlu, Ias on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47212770/
2 respondents in not complying with the order passed by this Court, amounts to willful default and violation of the order passed by this Court and therefore, the respondents are liable for punishment under the Contempt of Courts Act. 
8. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and perused the order in I.A.No.1 of 2017 (Rev.W.P.M.P.No.26423 of 2017) in W.P.No.8808 of 2016 and also the proceedings dated 02.09.2023 issued by the respondents.
6 AKS,J & RRN,J 9. In the review order, this Court, while allowing the review petition, set aside the order dated 28.04.2017 passed by this Court in W.P.No.8808 of 2016 as well as the order dated 20.08.2015 passed by the Tribunal in O.A.No.4438 of 2015 and the reversion order dated 01.04.2015 passed by the Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare. Pursuant to the review order passed by this Court,
the respondents have issued proceedings dated 02.09.2023.
10. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that under the proceedings dated 02.09.2023, the respondents have not granted consequential benefits to the petitioner, though he is entitled to the same. 
11. In view of the above submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, we are of the considered view that if the petitioner has any grievance in respect of the proceedings dated 02.09.2023, he is at liberty to challenge the same before appropriate forum. 
7 AKS,J & RRN,J 12. Since the respondents have complied with the order passed by this Court, this Court considers that there is no willful default on the part of the respondents in complying with the review order passed by this Court. 
13. Accordingly, the Contempt Case is closed. However, the petitioner is given the liberty to challenge the proceedings dated 02.09.2023 before the appropriate forum, if he is so aggrieved. 
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed. 
_________________________________ ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J _____________________________________ NAMAVARAPU RAJESHWAR RAO, J Date:
